about: How an ALTER COLUMN … TYPE <target> behaves on PostgreSQL 18, classified by the TARGET type. The source type is not in the migration SQL, so this is a heuristic keyed on the target and its dominant real case — the rule that reads it declares confidence=heuristic. A target listed under rewrite forces a full-table rewrite under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE from any type it is not binary-coercible from (the common case for these). A target under metadata_only is the dominant free change (varchar→text). A target under narrowing is one whose dominant real case is a narrowing of range or precision (integer from bigint, smallint, real from double precision) — read by the level-4 compatibility rule, which is a separate axis from rewrite. A target not listed under rewrite or metadata_only is an unknown transition and yields undetermined, never a silent pass. Parametrized narrowings (varchar(255)→varchar(50), smaller numeric precision) cannot be told from widenings by the target alone and are not classified here; that change already surfaces as an undetermined on the rewrite axis. A USING clause forces a rewrite regardless of the target and is handled by the rule, not this table. Aliases fold to their canonical PostgreSQL spelling before lookup.
